newsitem.title: CANADA: CBRS lowers unsecured Teleglobe Canada debt.
newsitem.headline: CBRS lowers unsecured Teleglobe Canada debt.

text.p: Canadian Bond Rating Service said on Friday that it downgraded the unsecured debentures of Teleglobe Canada Inc, the wholly owned operating unit of Teleglobe Inc.
CBRS said Teleglobe Canada's commercial paper rating has been reaffirmed at A-1, and the company's rating outlook remains stable.

The rating agency said the downgrade of Teleglobe Canada long term debt reflects the growing business and market risk facing the company with projections for increased leverage and reduced coverage ratios.

In 1996, Teleglobe Canada moved from rate of return regulation to a price-cap regime which allowed the company more operating and financial flexibility, but also exposed it to greater risks which could result in volatility in earnings and coverage ratios, CBRS said.
In the first nine months of 1996, Teleglobe Canada increased its debt to equity ratio to 43:57 percent from 40:60 percent, negatively affecting its strong coverage ratios, the agency said.

Longer term, the company will face growing competitive and market risks because of expected deregulation of its monopoly frnachise and general unpredictability of the global telecommunications industry. Despite the downgrade, Teleglobe Canada's ratings remain of good quality due to its strong market and satisfactory financial profile, CBRS said.
